items.title: South Central 93: Could AI destroy humanity? What’s happening in Telangana politics?
items.summary: Could AI really threaten humanity by the end of this decade, or are tech companies using the fear of AI to push for more control over the technology? In this week's South Central, hosts Dhanya Rajendran and Pooja Prasanna explore whether AI could pose an existential threat to humanity, and what regulation and the debate over whether AI development needs to slow down. They are joined by Sarayu Natarajan, founder of Aapti Institute and Visiting Associate Professor at Nanyang Technological University, Singapore, and Deepthi Bathini, AI Policy and Strategy Fellow at Successif and Associate Lecturer at Anglia Ruskin University, to discuss growing concerns around artificial intelligence, the risks posed by increasingly capable AI systems, calls for a slowdown in AI development, and the challenges of regulating the technology globally. Sarayu urges caution against treating every dramatic claim about AI as settled fact. She argues that while AI’s capabilities are rapidly advancing, the conversation is also shaped by marketing, billion-dollar valuations and geopolitical competition, making it important to separate the technology itself from the hype surrounding it. items.title: TERES joins Singapore Courts’ approved list for real-time transcription services
items.summary: Legal technology company TERES has been included in the Singapore Courts’ list of approved providers of real-time transcription services. The approval allows TERES to provide such services for hearings before the Supreme Court, including the Court of Appeal, the High Court and the Singapore International Commercial Court, as well as the State Courts and the Family Justice Courts. Speaking to Bar & Bench , TERES Chief Executive Officer Vikas Mahendra said the company was included on the list after a formal due diligence process carried out by the Singapore Courts. “ Representatives of the court had the opportunity to view our offering during the TechLaw.Fest in Singapore in 2024. This was followed by a formal process of due diligence carried out by the courts after which we were included ,” Mahendra said. items.title: Theja Rio’s Angh set in Nagaland gets prestigious Platform Prize at Toronto Film Festival
items.summary: From a small Indian state with virtually no formal film industry and the rugged mountains of indigenous tribes comes a historic moment. Marking its debut at the Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF), Angh , from Nagaland, clinched the prestigious Platform Prize on September 21. The prize ensures direct eligibility for submission to the Academy Awards 2027. As per TIFF and the Academy's rules , a non-English language film that wins the Platform Prize can be submitted for consideration for Best International Feature Film. Helming Angh is London-based 31-year-old Nagaland native Theja Rio, making a remarkably striking feature directorial debut. Angh explores the identity crisis of a Konyak tribal leader in Nagaland. The film triumphed over works by eleven world-renowned directors for the Platform Prize. The section featured 12 handpicked entries selected from over 4000 submissions across nearly 90 countries. Set in the 1960s in a Naga village bordering former Burma, the film unfolds as an American missionary arrives in the community. items.title: Forcing parties into mediation is always a bad idea: Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani
items.summary: Forcing parties into mediation is always a bad idea and there is no universally right stage at which parties must attempt settlement, Delhi High Court judge Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani said at the Commercial Mediation Conclave 2026. Speaking at the event, organised by The PACT and Poovayya & Co, Justice Bhambhani said the appropriate stage for mediation would depend on the nature of the dispute and the parties’ genuine willingness to explore a settlement. “I think what is or is not the right time to start mediation depends on the dispute. Forcing parties to mediation is always a bad idea. There are times when parties have been in litigation for very long, they have suffered the battle fatigue and all of that, the litigation fatigue and that's when it dawns on them that maybe we have been walking the wrong road .” He added that parties may become more receptive to mediation once the strengths and weaknesses of their respective cases become clearer. In disputes involving continuing commercial relationships, such as construction contracts, parties may also have practical reasons to preserve their association. At his farewell function on September 17, Justice Singh also revealed that he and his wife Shivati Indra Singh have pledged to donate their bodies to a medical college after their deaths for scientific purposes. The announcement came as Justice Singh reflected on his 37 years of service, the people who shaped his career and the principles he carried with him as a judge. items.title: Suspended directors have to give confidentiality undertaking for access to resolution plan: NCLAT
items.summary: The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) has held that a resolution professional can ask suspended directors to furnish a confidentiality undertaking before providing them access to a resolution plan and other confidential material in a corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP) [Mandava Prabhakar Rao Vs Navneet Gupta]. Technical Member Naresh Salecha , who was called upon to resolve an earlier split verdict by the NCLAT, agreed with the view that such a requirement does not violate the rights of suspended directors to participate CIRP. “ The resolution professional can take an undertaking from members of the erstwhile board of directors to maintain confidentiality, ” Salecha held. He said that the right of suspended directors to access resolution plans has to operate alongside their obligation to maintain confidentiality. The ruling arose from appeals filed by Mandava Prabhakar Rao, a suspended director of NSL Nagapatnam Power and Infratech Limited. The dispute concerned the company's 20th Committee of Creditors (CoC) meeting held on July 16, 2024. Rao had nominated Nelluri Bapuji to represent the suspended management in CoC meetings. items.title: Delhi High Court pulls up Delhi government over shortage of doctors, qualified staff in city hospitals
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Friday pulled up the Delhi government for not recruiting the necessary qualified doctors and staff at government hospitals. A bench of Justice Prathiba M Singh and Justice Manmeet Pritam Singh Arora noted that due to the inadequate recruitment of qualified staff, valuable equipment was also going unused. "There are no technicians running these equipments. The court is completely dissatisfied with the report placed on record. The hospitals are facing enormous difficulty in recruiting the necessary doctors and the staff. There is no uniform HR policy of the Delhi Government," the Court said. Justice Prathiba M Singh and Justice Manmeet Pritam Singh Arora The Court went on to observe, “ Judges will come, judges will go, but the hospitals have to function ." The Court was hearing a suo motu case in which it routinely monitors healthcare services in the city's government hospitals. On August 7 , the Court had expressed shock after being informed that 400 ventilators and 910 oxygen concentrators are lying unused at Guru Teg Bahadur (GTB) Hospital. items.title: New bench, old battle: Maratha reservation case to be reheard for third time by Bombay High Court
items.summary: The legal challenge to Maharashtra’s 2024 Maratha reservation law will be reheard for a third time by the Bombay High Court starting October 9. The challenge to the Act was earlier heard by a bench led by then Acting Chief Justice RV Ghuge . However following his elevation as the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court, a new bench has been formed which will now hear the matter afresh. The new bench is now headed by Justice MS Karnik ; Justices NJ Jamadar and SV Marne who were part of the earlier bench have been retained on the new bench. Justices NJ Jamadar, MS Karnik and SV Marne The bench will start hearing the petitions from October 9. It is a complete reset of the final arguments after almost 20 sittings, which began in June 2025. The Maharashtra State Reservation for Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (SEBC) Act, 2024 grants 10 percent reservation to the Maratha community in education and public employment. The challenge to this Act has faced continuous procedural resets. items.title: DHJS officer Reetesh Singh appointed new Registrar General of Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has appointed Delhi Higher Judicial Service (DHJS) officer Reetesh Singh as its new registrar general. At present, Singh is posted as Principal Secretary (Law, Justice and Legislative Affairs), Government of NCT of Delhi. "Hon'ble the Chief Justice has been pleased to appoint Mr. Reetesh Singh, an Officer of Delhi Higher Judicial Service, presently posted as Principal Secretary (Law, Justice and Legislative Affairs), Govt. of NCT of Delhi, as Registrar General in this Court on deputation basis, with effect from 22.09.2026," read a notification issued by the High Court. Singh has been given the assignment after the elevation of the High Court's former registrar general Arun Bhardwaj as an additional judge of the High Court. Bhardwaj took oath of office on September 21. [Read Notification]

The Court added that it may disturb the peaceful and harmonious atmosphere of a working place. items.title: Fair complexion, height, physique, English proficiency can't prove person follows Christianity: Madras High Court
items.summary: The Madras High Court recently held that the fair complexion of a person, tall height, good physique, and proficiency in Tamil and English are not reasons to claim that the person practices Christianity [ M Ravikumar v District Level Vigilance Committee & Ors. ]. Justice D Bharatha Chakravarthy made the observation while setting aside a District Level Vigilance Committee order which had rejected the community certificate of one M Ravikumar, a Customs Department officer. Ravikumar had claimed to belong to the Hindu Adi Dravidar community after being reconverted to Hinduism, following his birth into a Christian family.
